lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Anthropic says Opus 5.5 is forty percent cheaper. I checked the bill.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: KAXO's company is staffed entirely by Claude agents.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Anthropic released Opus 5.5, and KAXO had one question.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Is it worth the upgrade? Or is it just a bigger number?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So his employees ran the test for him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 got the exact same job.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Same instructions, same data, same hidden tests at the end.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: I'll make the call. Right after someone makes it for me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: We timed both runs to the second.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One finished five times faster than the other.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Five times. Somebody checked. Not me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: We also pulled each run's cost from the logs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Anthropic's number is forty. We got our own.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the slower model did something the fast one skipped.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: My verdict's at the end. It's my only job.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Both built this: a dashboard of KAXO's own company.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: It's mostly charts of other people working.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before any testing, here's Anthropic's official promise.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The token price drops twenty percent.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Cheaper employees. My favorite kind.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Input goes from five dollars per million tokens to four.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Output drops from twenty-five dollars to twenty.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Cached reads get sixty percent cheaper.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And on typical workloads, they say forty percent cheaper overall.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Twenty percent off, then forty percent off.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: I did the math. Everything's basically free now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They don't stack.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The forty is their estimate for typical work.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody's giving KAXO anything for free.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Rude.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Output should also be over thirty percent faster.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On Terminal-Bench 4.0, the score jumps from fifty-two to sixty-six.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: OSWorld goes from seventy-four to almost eighty-two.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Those numbers come from Anthropic's own page.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Benchmarks are job interviews. Everyone's great at interviews.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Here's the catch with price per token.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A job can take ten thousand tokens, or a million.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Price per finished job is what you actually pay.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: So I wanted a real job. And a real receipt.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The job came from KAXO's real office.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every time an agent there uses a tool, it gets logged.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That log had ninety-six events in it.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Ninety-six. Way too long to read.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The task: turn that log into a dashboard, in one HTML file.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No libraries, no internet, dark theme.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It gets screenshotted, so it has to look good.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Looking good is also my whole job.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The page needs events, tool calls, sessions, subagents, and the busiest hour.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Plus a sorted tool table and a bar chart.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One more number: KAXO's productivity, fixed by the spec at zero percent.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Finally, a metric that's accurate.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the important part: hidden tests.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They knew they'd be tested, but never saw how.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: I love secrets. Less talking.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Eighteen checks ran after both models finished.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Some use the real log, others use fake data built to break.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Built to break things. My kind of data.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One warning before the race.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's one task, run once per model, not a benchmark.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Both ran in Claude Code, on default settings.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: One roll of the dice. Like most of my business decisions.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They started at the same moment, in separate folders.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5.5 read the spec, wrote the page, and checked the numbers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Fifty-three seconds, done.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: I can't pick lunch in fifty-three seconds.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: This is the actual code Opus 5.5 wrote.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Five steps in total.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Meanwhile, Opus 5 was still going.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: I started a stopwatch. That was my contribution.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: This run would take thirty-one steps.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It wrote the page, then opened it in a browser.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then it tested four edge cases of its own.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Checking your own work. Bold move.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Four minutes and twenty-five seconds after the start, it finished.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: I napped through most of it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Here's where the gap came from.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every step, the model rereads its whole context.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: More steps means more rereading, and rereading costs money.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5 reread about one point three million cached tokens.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: One point three million. I've read maybe four.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5.5 reread about a hundred and twenty-eight thousand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Roughly ten times less.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Fewer steps, fewer rereads, smaller bill.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: One reads the manual every single step.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: The other skims. I respect that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now, the hidden tests.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5 passed eighteen out of eighteen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And Opus 5.5? Also eighteen out of eighteen.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Perfect scores, both of them. So nobody's fired.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: I was ready to fire someone. Mentally.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The real numbers matched on both pages.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ninety-six events, seventy tool calls, five sessions.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And KAXO's productivity, correctly, at zero percent.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Correctly. Twice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then, the bill.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Claude Code logs what each run would cost on the API.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For Opus 5, about a dollar forty-five.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5.5 came to twenty-seven cents.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Twenty-seven cents. I've lost more in the couch.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's eighty-one percent cheaper. Anthropic said forty.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: We ran it on a subscription, so no extra money changed hands.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Zero extra. My favorite price.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Our gap is bigger than the claim, and it's one run.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5.5 took six times fewer steps.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's the difference.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A different task could look very different.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Fine. Now the pretty part.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tests can't measure how a page looks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5 filled the whole screen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Vertical bars, value labels, tiny bars inside the table.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Fancy.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5.5 went clean and readable, with a share column.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But half its chart panel sits empty.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: About a hundred and ten pixels sit blank at the bottom.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: I'd have given both a ten. Didn't look.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Our QA agent did look.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nine out of ten for Opus 5, seven for Opus 5.5.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Harsh. Accurate, but harsh.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One more difference.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5.5 never opened its page in a browser.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It checked the numbers with a script and called it done.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And it said so openly.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: It skipped checking its own work. I've never felt so seen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: QA also hunted for edge cases the tests missed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It found one in Opus 5.5.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: The cheap one has a bug. Shocking.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: An empty tool name gets counted but never appears in the table.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the totals don't add up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5 had one too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: With forty different tools, its side panel runs off screen.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: So, a tie. In bugs too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Neither case was in the real data.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Opus 5 checked its work, but left a mess behind.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Draft scripts and screenshots stayed in its folder.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: To be fair, it wasn't allowed to delete files.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Not allowed to clean up. I use that excuse too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: KAXO, upgrade or not?

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Upgrade. Five times faster, for a fraction of the price.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: And the checking it skips? QA does that anyway.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Fast worker, careful checker. And me, supervising from the couch.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: If looks are the whole job, Opus 5 earned its extra dollar.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Oh, and both were told to reply in one line.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Neither did.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: At least they reply. I don't.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One job, one run: a data point, not a law.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every number's source, including Anthropic's page, is in the description.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Want a rematch on a harder task? Tell us in the comments.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: Anthropic said forty percent cheaper.

lines.speaker: kaxo
lines.text: My bill said eighty-one percent. For one job.
